newsitem.title: GERMANY: German construction demand still pressured - HDB.
newsitem.headline: German construction demand still pressured - HDB.

text.p: The German construction industry is likely to remain under pressure even though the west German commercial sector showed considerable gains in April, an industry group said on Tuesday.

Construction demand in west Germany rose a real five percent in April, driven by a 13.2 percent increase in orders for commercial construction, the Association of the German Construction Industry (HDB) reported.
But a particularly weak first quarter and further setbacks in eastern Germany damped order totals for the first four months of the year.
"It is too early to speak of a change in the trend in the west Germany construction market," HDB said in a statement.

The group said a weak housing outlook limited the industry's prospects. Permits for single- and two-family homes in west Germany fell 5.4 percent in April and 18.2 percent in January-April, both from the year-earlier period.
Total west German orders in the four-month period fell a real four percent. In the east, orders fell 15.7 percent in April, and 11.4 percent in the first four months.

West German public works demand rose in April, as orders climbed 4.9 percent, but the January-April total was flat. Orders for homes fell a real 5.8 percent in April, and 9.7 percent in the first four months of the year.

In east Germany, commercial construction demand fell 16.9 percent in April while orders in the first four months dropped 15.4 percent. Public works orders fell 8.2 percent in April and 13.9 percent in the January-April period.
Home construction demand in the east fell 20.9 percent in April, but was down only 4.8 percent for the first four months of 1997.
Public works construction in the east was down 8.2 percent in April and 13.9 percent for January through April.
The number of west German construction jobs in April was 817,000, up 3.6 percent month-on-month but 10.3 percent below the level of April 1996.
HDB said it expected the loss of another 42,000 jobs in west Germany this year. It also forecast investment in the region would fall one to two percent in 1997.

In east Germany, there were 359,000 construction jobs in April, down 10.9 percent month-on-month. HDB expected the loss of 38,000 more jobs this year and predicted east German construction investment would fall three to four percent.
